title: Wicklow Granite: Dublin Mountains to Lugnaquilla

bestPeriod.window: May to early October. May-June for long light and drier bog; September for firm ground and heather; avoid February-March when the peat is saturated

transport.note: €120-200: car hire €45-60 per day, or St Kevin's Bus and DART if going car-free

profile.difficultyNote: Moderate-hard. Not alpine, but relentlessly boggy; navigation on featureless plateaux is the real skill and Lugnaquilla in cloud is genuinely serious

summary: A seven-day trail running itinerary in County Wicklow / Dublin Mountains, Ireland.

itinerary.title: Arrive Dublin, Bray Head to Greystones
itinerary.morning: Fly into Dublin, DART train south to Bray, 45 minutes, right along the coast.
itinerary.afternoon: The Bray Head cliff path to Greystones: sea on one side, gorse on the other, a runnable 7 km with an optional climb to the cross on Bray Head (241 m). DART back from Greystones.
itinerary.evening: Fish and chips in Bray, then transfer inland to your Wicklow base. **Water:** town taps at both ends; carry a flask.

itinerary.title: Great Sugar Loaf and Djouce
itinerary.morning: Great Sugar Loaf (501 m) is a 45-minute quartzite cone from the Red Lane car park, steep, scree-topped, and the finest small hill in Ireland for effort-to-view ratio.
itinerary.afternoon: Move to the Wicklow Way at Crone Wood: the loop past Powerscourt Waterfall, Ireland's highest at 121 m, then up to Maulin and along the boardwalk over White Hill to Djouce (725 m), with Lough Tay, the "Guinness Lake", black below.
itinerary.evening: Roundwood, Ireland's highest village, and a pub dinner. **Water:** the Dargle stream below Powerscourt Waterfall; the Djouce boardwalk section is dry.

itinerary.title: Glendalough Spinc and Camaderry loop
itinerary.morning: From the Upper Lake car park, the railway-sleeper boardwalk climbs to the Spinc ridge above the Glendalough valley, the classic view down onto the monastic city and both lakes.
itinerary.afternoon: Extend north over Camaderry (700 m) on open bog, then descend the miners' road past the abandoned lead workings at Glendasan. Finish through the 6th-century monastic settlement with its round tower.
itinerary.evening: Glendalough. Early dinner; tomorrow is the long one. **Water:** the Glenealo river above the miners' village is excellent; the boardwalk ridge has none.

itinerary.title: Lugnaquilla, the county top
itinerary.morning: Lugnaquilla is 925 m and the highest mountain in Ireland outside Kerry. **Critical rule: the western approach through the Glen of Imaal crosses a live Defence Forces artillery range.** Check the published firing notices before you go, and if in doubt use the eastern approach from Glenmalure instead. `verify: true`
itinerary.afternoon: From Baravore in Glenmalure, climb through Fraughan Rock Glen, a hanging valley with waterfalls, onto the plateau. The summit is a broad flat dome called the Percy's Table with cliffs (the North and South Prisons) on either side; in cloud, navigate on a bearing and do not shortcut.
itinerary.evening: Glenmalure Lodge for food and a fire. This is the deepest glacial valley in Ireland and there is no phone signal at the head of it. **Water:** the Avonbeg river and the Fraughan Rock Glen streams, abundant and clean.

itinerary.title: Tonelagee, Lough Ouler and the Wicklow Gap
itinerary.morning: From the Wicklow Gap road, up Tonelagee (817 m). Lough Ouler sits in its northeast corrie in the shape of a heart, Wicklow's most photographed corrie lake, and it is a run, not a climb.
itinerary.afternoon: Traverse toward Turlough Hill and the pumped-storage reservoir on top, then down the Glenmacnass valley past the waterfall. The bog between Tonelagee and Turlough Hill is the deepest on this itinerary; keep to the peat ridges.
itinerary.evening: Laragh village. **Water:** Glenmacnass river; Lough Ouler's outflow.

itinerary.title: Mullaghcleevaun and the high bog crossing
itinerary.morning: Mullaghcleevaun (849 m), Wicklow's second summit, from the Oasis car park on the military road. Long featureless plateau running; this is the day you find out whether you can navigate.
itinerary.afternoon: Return via Duff Hill and Gravale on a rough line, or drop to the Sally Gap and run the military road, built by the British after 1798 to open the mountains, and now the loneliest tarmac in Leinster.
itinerary.evening: Return to Dublin, or a last night in Enniskerry. If it is a summer weekday evening, enter an **IMRA** race, the Irish Mountain Running Association runs a weekly midweek series across these hills, entry is a few euro on the night, and it is the fastest way into the local scene. `verify: true` **Water:** the Cleevaun Lough outflow; the plateau is otherwise a bog with no running water.

itinerary.title: Dublin shakeout and out
itinerary.morning: Easy 8 km around Phoenix Park, 707 hectares, twice the size of Central Park, with a resident fallow deer herd, or the Howth cliff loop if you prefer sea air.
itinerary.afternoon: Dublin Airport, 30 minutes from the city.

accommodationStrategy.name: Glenmalure Lodge
accommodationStrategy.description: An old coaching inn at the head of Ireland's deepest glacial valley, right at the Lugnaquilla and Fraughan Rock Glen trailheads. Rooms are simple; the location is unbeatable and the kitchen serves late enough for a slow day on the hill. No mobile coverage, tell someone your plan before you drive in.

accommodationStrategy.name: Wicklow Way Lodge / Roundwood-area B&Bs
accommodationStrategy.description: Purpose-built for walkers and runners, with drying space, early breakfasts and lifts to trailheads by arrangement. Central for Days 2, 3 and 5, and 30 minutes from the Sally Gap.

accommodationStrategy.name: Glendalough International Hostel (An Óige)
accommodationStrategy.description: Inside the national park beside the monastic site, with a kitchen and secure storage. Cheapest way to run the Spinc at dawn before the coach parties arrive at 10:00, which is the single best hour of the week.

logistics.connectivity: Good in the valleys and towns, absent on the plateaux and in Glenmalure. Download OSI 1:50,000 or OS Maps offline layers before you leave Dublin.
logistics.emergency: 112 or 999, ask for **Mountain Rescue**. Dublin and Wicklow Mountain Rescue covers these hills. Register your route with someone; there is no signal in Glenmalure, at the head of Glenmacnass, or on much of the Mullaghcleevaun plateau.
logistics.weather: Wicklow is only 900 m high but Atlantic cloud sits on the plateaux for days. The classic accident is a competent runner navigating off a featureless summit in 30 m visibility. Carry map, compass and the ability to use them, a phone with a dead battery in horizontal rain is not a navigation system.
logistics.bookingWindows: Glendalough and Glenmalure accommodation: 6-8 weeks for summer weekends. Car hire in Ireland: book early and read the insurance excess terms closely, Irish CDW rules differ from mainland Europe. `verify: true`

other.label: Live firing
other.text: The Glen of Imaal artillery range is active and marked with red flags and warning signs. Firing schedules are published in advance. Never cross a marked range boundary, never pick up metal objects, and use the Glenmalure or Camara Hill approaches when firing is scheduled. `verify: true`

other.label: Bog craft
other.text: After heavy rain, the peat between Tonelagee and Turlough Hill and around Duff Hill will take you to mid-thigh. Follow the drier heather ridges, not the direct line, and expect 30-50% slower splits than the distance suggests.

other.label: Access
other.text: Ireland has no general right to roam; upland access is by long-standing tolerance, not law. Close gates, never cross a field with livestock, and park only in designated car parks, the Wicklow parking situation at Glendalough and Sally Gap is a live local grievance.

proTips: Run the **Spinc at 07:00**. The Glendalough Upper Lake car park fills by 10:00 in summer and the boardwalk becomes a queue; at dawn the valley is yours and the light comes down the lake.
Enter a midweek **IMRA** race. It costs less than a pint, the courses are the local secret lines you would never find on a map, and the pub afterwards will tell you exactly which bog to avoid.
The **Military Road** over Sally Gap is the best warm-down drive in Ireland and the worst place to break down. Fuel up in Laragh or Enniskerry.
Two-car logistics unlock the good linear routes. Leave a car at Glenmalure and run Wicklow Way sections point-to-point instead of doing out-and-backs.
**Guinness Lake (Lough Tay) is private land**, the viewpoint from the R759 is the legal one, and the drone-shot angle everyone chases is not.

Pack for water, not for cold. Wicklow rarely goes below 5 °C in season but it will soak you completely; a waterproof with a stiff hood brim and spare dry socks in a bag beats an extra insulating layer.

raw.water_strategy: Wicklow's upland streams run off granite and blanket bog, clear, peat-brown and generally safe above grazing, but filter anything below a sheep line
